title: Extend `datetime` attribute on <time> to support Temporal ZonedDateTime timezone syntax

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

## Summary

This is a focused proposal  split from my earlier issue to extend the existing `datetime` attribute on `<time>` to accept a timezone identifier using Temporal's ZonedDateTime syntax, enabling timezone-aware time display without JavaScript.

---

## Background

This proposal was shaped by feedback from the community suggesting that rather than introducing a new `timezone` attribute, it would be cleaner to extend the existing `datetime` attribute using Temporal's ZonedDateTime syntax for example `datetime="[Asia/Karachi]"`. This keeps the proposal aligned with existing standards.

---

## The Problem

Today, showing time in a specific timezone requires verbose JavaScript:

```javascript
new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
  timeZone: 'Asia/Karachi',
  hour: '2-digit',
  minute: '2-digit',
  second: '2-digit',
  hour12: true
}).format(new Date());
```

This is boilerplate that every developer repeats. There is no declarative way to express timezone intent in HTML markup.

---

## Proposed Solution

Extend the `datetime` attribute to accept a Temporal ZonedDateTime timezone identifier in brackets:

```html
<!-- Pakistan Standard Time -->
<time datetime="[Asia/Karachi]"></time>

<!-- New York -->
<time datetime="[America/New_York]"></time>

<!-- Combined with live attribute (separate proposal) -->
<time live datetime="[Asia/Karachi]"></time>
```

---

## Why Temporal ZonedDateTime Syntax?

- Temporal API is already advancing in browsers this aligns with that direction
- IANA timezone identifiers are well-established and unambiguous
- Bracket syntax `[Asia/Karachi]` already exists in Temporal no new convention needed
- Avoids introducing a brand new `timezone` attribute

---

## Open Questions

- Should this only work alongside the `live` attribute or also for static time display?
- How should fallback rendering work when Temporal is not yet supported?
- Should format control (12hr vs 24hr) also be declarable perhaps via a `format` attribute?

Open to all feedback. Thanks for considering this.
